newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toshiba plan to lower chip investment plan - paper.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba plan to lower chip investment plan - paper.

text.p: Major semiconductor chip maker Toshiba Corp plans to lower its capital investment for its semiconductor business in the year to March 31, 1997, and other chip makers, including NEC Corp and Hitachi Ltd, are expected to follow suit, a Japanese newspaper said on Wednesday.

Toshiba plans the revision because of the sluggish market of 16 megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips due to oversupply of the product, the economic daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said. Toshiba spokesmen were not immediately available for comment on the report.

Toshiba originally planned group investment in chip-producing plants and equipment of 180 billion yen but will lower that to 170 billion yen, the paper said. Its chip output in 1996/97 should be worth 950 billion yen, down from its original estimate of 1.05 trillion yen, the paper said.

NEC will cut its investment in chip facilities in 1996/97 by 10 to 20 billion yen from its original plan of 210 billion yen, the paper said. Hitachi will cut its investment by 10 to 20 billion yen from its original plan of 175 billion yen and Fujitsu Ltd is also expected to cut its investment in chip facilities, the paper said.
